About the Veterinary Science event

Veterinary Science is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Veterinary Science 2026–27 test plan for large and small animals (anatomy and physiology 24%, diseases 14%, emergency care 12%, surgery 12%, nutrients 10%, clinical practice 10%, behavior, zoonoses and ethics 6% each) and all seven Round Two skills: instrument and breed identification, operative site preparation, fecal flotation, lifting and restraining a dog, wrapping a surgical pack and cat-friendly handling. Built around Lawhead and Baker’s Introduction to Veterinary Science, the Red Cross Pet First Aid app and AKC and CFA breed standards, with vital-sign tables, species-term matching, parasite and toxin sorting, breed and instrument drills and step-ordering for every rating sheet. Round Two uses stuffed animals; always follow the scenario you are given.

Veterinary Science lessons

Test plan: ethics, legal and safety 6%; anatomy and physiology 24%.

Test plan: clinical practice 10%, emergency care 12%. Skills IV, V and VII.

  1. Clinical practice: examinations, restraint and feline handling (Skills V and VII) 30 min

  2. Laboratory procedures and fecal flotation (Skill IV) 30 min

Sample Veterinary Science questions

1. Dogs and cats walk on their toes rather than on the soles of their feet. What is this type of stance called?

  1. Digitigrade
  2. Plantigrade
  3. Unguligrade
  4. Bipedal
Show answer

A. Digitigrade

Humans and bears are plantigrade (whole sole), horses are unguligrade (tip of the hoof), and dogs and cats are digitigrade.

2. Why is an Elizabethan collar (cone) used after surgery?

  1. To help the animal breathe
  2. To keep the animal warm
  3. To support the neck muscles after surgery
  4. To prevent licking the incision
Show answer

D. To prevent licking the incision

Licking and chewing can introduce bacteria or remove sutures.

3. Before treating an injured dog, why might a muzzle be applied?

  1. To keep the dog warm
  2. Pain can make even a gentle dog bite
  3. To stop the dog from barking
  4. To help the dog breathe
Show answer

B. Pain can make even a gentle dog bite

A muzzle protects the rescuer but must not be used if the dog is vomiting, having trouble breathing or has a mouth injury.
